title: Depth-Progressive Monotonic Learning without Global Backpropagation
claim: Conventionally trained networks collapse when depth is altered mid-training and recover slowly, while our method stays stable and recovers instantly.
layout: 1 panel, line plot split into three shaded phase regions with callout arrows
description: A single line chart of test accuracy (%) against training epochs (1–60), divided by dotted vertical lines into three shaded phases. Phase 1 (grey, 6 modules) covers the deep network, Phase 2 (pink, 4 modules) is the depth cut, and Phase 3 (green, 6 modules) is the deep return. Four curves are shown: BP with skip probability 0.5 (red dashed), BP with skip probability 0.1 (orange solid), DMoL with skip probability 0.1 (thick blue solid) and DMoL with skip probability 0.5 (teal dashed). At the Phase 2 boundary both BP curves plunge to near zero, while the DMoL curves stay at about 55%. Colored arrows and labels mark 'BP Collapse (Feature Mismatch)', 'DMoL Stability (Decoupled Inference)', 'DMoL Hot-Swap (Instant Recovery)' and 'BP Retraining (Slow Adaptation)'. A boxed legend sits at the bottom left. The eye goes first to the sharp BP drop in the pink region.
caption: Structural Fragility Test under Stochastic Skipping. We train models with random module skipping (Phase 1) and simulate dynamic removal of intermediate modules (Phase 2), and reinstate the removed modules (Phase 3). BP suffers catastrophic collapse when depth is altered. In contrast, our proposed DMoL exhibits strong stability and instant recovery.
abstract: Backpropagation (BP) remains the dominant training paradigm for deep neural networks, yet its reliance on global gradient propagation fundamentally induces update locking problem, enforcing strong inter-layer dependencies in parameter updates. To address this limitation, we propose Depth-progressive Monotonic Learning (DMoL), a training scheme that assigns layer-wise local belief objectives and incrementally refines them across network depth, enabling unlocked parameter updates. As a result, DMoL supports dynamic modification of network depth during training, adapting to available compute and device resources while maintaining stable optimization. We provide theoretical guarantees that layer-wise local belief objectives improve monotonically with increasing depth and converge exponentially. Empirically, DMoL consistently matches or outperforms BP across diverse tasks, yielding a 4.3\% accuracy gain on CIFAR-100, mitigating over-smoothing in deep graph neural networks (+37.5\% on Cora), and reducing the final loss by over 35\% in diffusion model training, highlighting its robustness and flexibility as an alternative to BP. The code is publicly available at: https://github.com/ychAlbert/DMoL.
